I'm very partial to the tri-vagal theory of the human nervous system. Basically, we intereact with one another socially in order to co-regulate each other's stress responses/hormones. The world is fear and trembling. We take it very for granted, even being able to maintain any sense of safety and sanity in it. The vagal nerve is massive and is distributed on both the ventral and dorsal sides of the body. The dorsal side activation produces a dissociative response (those moments when you tune out of a social setting and shut down; this is a stress response). The ventral side positively regulates your emotions and stress response. Positive interactions activate the ventral vagal and give your nervous system and mind the experience of being safe and secure; so you open up because your world is interpreted as a place where it is okay to do that.

This is why people do small talk. It's just extending feelers out there and looking for a bit of positivity that will co-regulate their ongoing stress response and make them feel better about the world around them. So you are legitimately improving someone physically, mentally, and in their own ability to regulate others when you just take the small amount of effort to smile and say something positive to them. Make them laugh, or say something that isn't doom and gloom.

I have to disagree.

1st it does not look like an armored cable to me. When an armored cable breaks the armor frays. The outer jacket just looks like standard umbilical outer sheath for electronics transmission (power and data). No where in the article does it say that it was an armored or steel cable. Armored umbilicals are general not made of steels, as steel corrodes in salt water.

2nd trawlers and especially purse seiners can haul fish in by the ton, Here is some info from NOAA

https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/bycatch/fishing-gear-purse-seines

3rd I have seen all kinds of rigging pop, from wire slings to the big ass hawsers used on container ships.

4th it is totally possible that the equipment was snagged in a vessel's anchor. On larger vessels the anchors are winched up. This could have easily snapped the cable. Anchors on ships weigh tons, so the winch is quite capable of lifting 1500 lbs.

*** The article does not say why they think it was weather conditions? Slack reporting from shit CNN. Being they sent divers down to check it, I can guarantee that it was in a maximum of 30m or 100 ft of water.
